approach: Stop rewriting the local branch after a merge, so a running job's base stays an ancestor of HEAD and `plan` still lands it. Remove the `resync_onto_merge` call in `Athena::land_pr`, plus `resync_onto_merge` and `resync_tip`. Move the squash-conflict fix to the pull request head. At publish and replace time, `Remote::cut_head` replays the local landed commit onto the host's current default-branch tip. Commits that an earlier squash already carries replay to empty and are skipped, so each merge lands one job as one commit. The push guards use the cut commit as `local_head`. `PrLink.source` records the local commit the head was cut from, and reruns compare that source, so an unchanged source causes no push. A fingerprint mismatch or replay conflict pushes nothing and reports the job as stale. Docs say how outside changes on main reach the local branch.

decisions.choice: Dispatch from the local branch HEAD as today, but never rewrite that branch on merge; cut each pull request head onto the remote default tip at publish time.
decisions.reason: Dispatch records base_commit = head, and `plan` in land.rs needs the base to be an ancestor of HEAD. Only the resync breaks that on a merge. Removing it makes dispatch independent of any merge, and the replay primitive already exists.

rejected.option: Dispatch from a pinned ref such as origin/main or a new refs/athena/base
rejected.why: Job records are committed to the local branch and read from HEAD, so a second base would split the record history. Larger and riskier.

rejected.option: Keep resync but run it only when no job is running
rejected.why: That is the wait the request wants removed, and it needs a cross-process view of running jobs.

rejected.option: Merge the squash commit into the local branch
rejected.why: Adds merge commits, which violates one merge, one commit.

rejected.option: Re-cut the head on every `land --pr` rerun
rejected.why: Replay makes new timestamps, so each rerun would replace-push. Comparing the stored source avoids that.

decisions.choice: Add `source: Option<String>` (serde default) to PrLink and a defaulted `Remote::cut_head(base_branch, commit)` overridden by GitRemote. PushRequest/ReplaceRequest.local_head becomes the cut commit. The rerun comparison at gh.rs:1297 becomes `link.source.clone().unwrap_or(link.head) != job.commit`.
decisions.reason: check_push and check_replace (pr.rs) take local_head and today receive job.commit. After the cut, link.head is the cut commit, so comparing it to job.commit would re-cut on every rerun. A default that returns the commit unchanged keeps existing fakes and old links working.

rejected.option: Replay in Athena::land_pr before calling the flow
rejected.why: The default branch name is read inside publish, and the replace path needs the same cut. One place is easier to test.

decisions.choice: If the cut head's tree fingerprint differs from the verified one, or replay conflicts, push nothing and report the job as stale. Athena never merges it.
decisions.reason: Keeps P5 and the merged-unverified protection, and honors the out-of-scope on automatic merge or re-verification. This also covers an outside governed change on main: cuts are refused until the maintainer merges main into the local branch by hand (replay then rebuilds that as one change) or re-runs the job.

rejected.why: Out of scope. It would land content no verifier saw.

decisions.choice: Edit gh.rs although it is not a listed deliverable (finding 1), and flag it to the reviewer.
decisions.reason: The only resync call, the Remote trait, publish and replace_head live in gh.rs, so the fault cannot be fixed from the listed files alone. The edit is minimal. run.rs and watcher.rs get no logic change; a comment in run.rs only if useful, and watcher.rs only if a resync reference turns up.

rejected.option: Make resync_onto_merge a no-op in land.rs
rejected.why: Leaves dead code, and the squash-conflict fix still needs the cut in the publish flow.

decisions.choice: The criterion 1 test drives Athena::land_pr itself, with a fake Remote/host reporting A's PR merged with a side-ref squash commit (finding 2).
decisions.reason: The resync ran only inside land_pr after report.link.state == Landed. A test that only calls `plan` would pass either way.

rejected.option: Simulate the squash on a side ref and call only `plan`
rejected.why: Nothing rewrites HEAD with or without the resync call, so the test proves nothing.

risks.risk: A cut head carries different content than the verified landed commit.
risks.mitigation: Fingerprint check before any push. A mismatch or replay conflict pushes nothing and reports. The merged-unverified check stays.

risks.risk: Reruns re-cut and push a new head each time.
risks.mitigation: Store head and source in PrLink and compare source (fallback head) to job.commit. A test shows no push on an unchanged source.

risks.risk: Existing gh.rs fakes and tests break from the new trait method or field.
risks.mitigation: Defaulted method and serde default. Keep the 'rerun replaces a bare candidate head' test passing.

risks.risk: An outside change on main blocks every later cut, because the local branch never takes it in.
risks.mitigation: Refuse and report clearly. Docs tell the maintainer to merge main into the local branch by hand.
It drives land_pr, and the producer temporarily restores the resync call to confirm it fails.

demonstrations.method: A new test with a real git repo (Git::isolated) calls Athena::land_pr for job A with a fake host that reports A's PR as merged, returning a single-parent squash commit on a side ref. Job B was dispatched at base P before the merge. After land_pr returns, the test asserts on B and on the host side. The producer temporarily restores the resync call to confirm the test fails.
demonstrations.observes: Local HEAD id is identical before and after land_pr. B's base and worktree files are unchanged. P is still an ancestor of HEAD. `plan` for B returns Plan::Tree with the verified fingerprint, not Stale. B's head, cut after the merge, is a linear chain onto the squash commit with the same fingerprint, so its candidate lands cleanly.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the resync call in place, land_pr rewrites HEAD, so the HEAD-unchanged assertion fails and `plan` for B returns Stale.

demonstrations.method: A new gh.rs test with a bare remote and GitRemote. The local branch holds P, A's landed commit, a records commit, then B's landed commit, back to back before any merge. Cut A's head with cut_head, squash-merge A on the remote default branch, then cut B's head. Also run publish twice with an unchanged source and count pushes.
demonstrations.observes: Each cut head is a linear chain onto the then-current remote tip. `git rev-list --merges` is empty. B's head holds only B's own commits, not A's. Cut tree fingerprints equal the verified ones. The local branch tip is unchanged. The second publish with an unchanged source makes no push, and check_push/check_replace saw the cut commit as local_head.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the replay onto the remote tip, B's head would carry A's local commit, so the commit-count and merge-free assertions fail. Without the source comparison, the rerun pushes again.

demonstrations.method: Run the three checks over the whole workspace, including the new tests and the rewritten former resync tests.
demonstrations.observes: cargo test exits 0 with the new tests passing. `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check` also exit 0.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the resync call were removed but resync_tip/resync_onto_merge stayed, clippy -D warnings fails on dead code. If the cut or no-rewrite behavior were missing, the criterion 1 and 2 tests fail.

They also state that outside changes on main reach the local branch by a hand merge (replay rebuilds it as one change), that cuts are refused until then, and that replay cost is an estimate.
